title: TransMem — code view
subtitle: What the released repo (@ 6d7a612) actually executes at training time (5 separate entry scripts) and inference time (one forward hook on the last 4 layers). Same 4-lane-plus-boundary footprint as the paper view.
source: repo TransMem @ 6d7a612 (github.com/Haodong-Lei-Ray/TransMem, HEAD commit message "vanish")   ·   verified against servers/transmem/verification.md (71 code-side assertions: 51 correct / 1 wrong / 17 partial / 2 unverifiable)
footer: memory-bench · methodology flow · code view · every citation re-opened and confirmed during verification
legend_notes: The only real storage in the whole system is training-side: Stage-0 teacher-rollout .pt shards (extract_features.py atomic_save) and the mem-only checkpoint. Full-repo grep finds zero faiss/chromadb/bm25/networkx/neo4j dependencies — there is nothing to index or retrieve at inference time.

5 training entry points exist (train_inloop.py=ECSD headline, train_offpolicy.py=SFT, train_onpolicy.py=OPD, train_grpo.py+rl.py=GRPO, train_layered.py=archived v3), matching the paper's own Table 5 four-objective ablation — a confirmed match, not a divergence (D11).

The default shipped config (config_layered.json, gate_mode="constant") is weaker than any ablation the paper reports: it fixes the gate to g=1 AND only injects into layer 35 (Last-1, inject_layers:[35]) — reproducing the paper's headline Last-4 dynamic-gate number requires overriding both CONFIG and --inject_layers/-D by hand (C49/C68).

Memory-slot selection (Sched:MemSelect) defaults to hm_mode="floor", which can miss the context's true last token h_L by up to N-1 positions; the formula that actually matches the paper ("frac") is only ever forced on the rarely-triggered overflow path — see diff view D3.
